overall: Atlanta hit a running maximum of 91.4°F around 16:19 ET, exceeding all NWP model forecasts, before a sharp thunderstorm-driven temperature crash brought readings down to 80.6°F by 17:52 ET — a ~10°F drop in roughly one hour. Active severe weather is ongoing across the region (Tornado Warning, Severe Thunderstorm Warning, Severe Thunderstorm Watch all in effect), and the rapid cooling (-7.2°F/hr velocity as of 18:19 ET) is consistent with strong convective outflow. The diurnal warming window has fully closed.
forecast_obs_notes: All three NWP models (ECMWF=87.5°F, HRRR=89.6°F, NBM=86.8°F) underforecast the actual observed peak by 1.8–3.9°F, likely because they did not fully capture the intensity of afternoon heating before convective initiation. The intraday model correctly concentrated 96.8% probability in the 90–91°F bucket, and the give-up classifier fired at hour 14.67 with 92% confidence — both signals proved accurate.
max_temp_prediction: The daily high is effectively locked in at 91.4°F. Temperatures are plunging rapidly in the wake of thunderstorm passage, it is already 18:19 ET (past the diurnal peak by over two hours), and ongoing severe convection precludes any re-warming tonight. The running max has been stationary at 91.4°F since at least 17:00 ET with no upward movement. Confidence is very high (>95%) that TMAX will be officially recorded at or extremely close to 91.4°F.
